items.stem: Define the term 'human resource management (HRM)'.
items.answer: The strategic approach to managing the employees of a business, including workforce planning, recruitment, training, appraisal, pay and employee welfare.
items.markingKey: 2 marks: full definition – The strategic approach to managing the employees of a business, including workforce planning, recruitment, training, appraisal, pay and employee welfare. 1 mark: partial definition or a relevant example only. [2]

items.stem: Explain two roles of the human resources department.
items.answer: It plans the workforce and recruits and selects staff so the business has the right number of people with the right skills; and it trains and develops employees to improve their performance.
items.markingKey: 2 × (1 mark role, 1 mark explanation): workforce planning, recruitment/selection, training, appraisal, pay, welfare, discipline. [4]

items.stem: Explain the difference between hard HRM and soft HRM.
items.answer: Hard HRM treats employees as a resource to be used as cheaply and efficiently as possible, with short-term contracts and little involvement; soft HRM treats them as assets to be developed, motivated and involved in decisions.
items.markingKey: 1 mark hard HRM; 1 mark soft HRM; 1 mark contrast/example. [3]

items.stem: Based in Bogotá, Café Cordillera SAS (private limited company) roasts coffee and runs a chain of 60 cafés. The business has around 900 employees. The owners want to double the number of cafés within three years. Explain how the human resources department could help Café Cordillera to achieve its objectives.
items.answer: Points to develop for Café Cordillera: HRM manages the workforce strategically; workforce planning ensures the right number of staff with the right skills; training raises productivity and quality; good welfare and pay reduce labour turnover.
items.markingKey: AO1 Knowledge [1]: HRM manages the workforce strategically. AO2 Application [1]: point linked to Café Cordillera (food and drink retail). AO3 Analysis [1]: developed explanation of the consequence, e.g. workforce planning ensures the right number of staff with the right skills; training raises productivity and quality. [3]

items.stem: Based in Manila, IslaConnect Inc. (private limited company) runs customer-service call centres for banks and airlines in the USA and Australia. The business has around 2,600 employees. Clients are starting to replace human call handlers with artificial intelligence. Explain how the human resources department could help IslaConnect to achieve its objectives.
items.answer: Points to develop for IslaConnect: HRM manages the workforce strategically; workforce planning ensures the right number of staff with the right skills; training raises productivity and quality; good welfare and pay reduce labour turnover.
items.markingKey: AO1 Knowledge [1]: HRM manages the workforce strategically. AO2 Application [1]: point linked to IslaConnect (business process outsourcing). AO3 Analysis [1]: developed explanation of the consequence, e.g. workforce planning ensures the right number of staff with the right skills; training raises productivity and quality. [3]

items.stem: Based in Karachi, Indus Sports Goods Ltd (private limited company) makes hand-stitched and machine-stitched footballs and cricket equipment. The business has around 950 employees. A rival in China has started selling machine-made balls at lower prices. Evaluate whether a soft approach to HRM would be more effective than a hard approach for Indus Sports.
items.answer: For: motivation and loyalty; innovation from involved staff; lower labour turnover. Against: higher costs; hard HRM may suit routine, low-skilled work; competitive pressure to keep costs low. Judgement: for Indus Sports it depends mainly on the skills needed in sports equipment manufacturing, and also on the financial position.
items.markingKey: AO1 Knowledge [2]: relevant concepts. AO2 Application [2]: uses the evidence (Indus Sports: sports equipment manufacturing, about 950 employees, private limited company in Pakistan; a rival in China has started selling machine-made balls at lower prices). AO4 Evaluation [3]: a justified judgement that weighs the arguments, e.g. it depends on the skills needed in sports equipment manufacturing; the financial position; the management culture. A top-level answer reaches a supported conclusion specific to Indus Sports. [10]

items.markingKey: 1 mark: relevant disadvantage, e.g. higher training and welfare costs; decisions may take longer; benefits take time to appear. 1 mark: explained in the context of Lotus Spa (personal services). [2]

items.stem: Define the term 'workforce planning'.
items.answer: Analysing the current workforce and forecasting the number and skills of employees the business will need in the future.
items.markingKey: 2 marks: full definition – Analysing the current workforce and forecasting the number and skills of employees the business will need in the future. 1 mark: partial definition or a relevant example only. [2]

items.stem: Explain one advantage and one disadvantage of external recruitment.
items.answer: Advantage: it brings in new ideas and skills and a wider choice of candidates. Disadvantage: it is more expensive and slower, and the new employee needs longer induction.
items.markingKey: 1 mark advantage, 1 mark explanation; 1 mark disadvantage, 1 mark explanation. [4]

items.stem: Explain why a business should carry out workforce planning.
items.answer: It ensures the business has the right number of employees with the right skills when needed, avoiding shortages that reduce output or surpluses that raise costs, and allows time for recruitment and training.
items.markingKey: 1 mark right number/skills; 1 mark avoid shortage or surplus; 1 mark time to recruit/train. [3]

items.stem: Pearl Logistics is a private limited company in Doha, Qatar with about 1,500 staff. It provides freight forwarding, warehousing and lorry delivery services. items.answer: Points to develop for Pearl Logistics: workforce planning forecasts future labour needs; new skills may be needed, such as languages; time is needed to recruit and train staff; avoids costly shortages or surpluses of staff.
items.markingKey: AO1 Knowledge [1]: workforce planning forecasts future labour needs. AO2 Application [1]: point linked to Pearl Logistics (logistics). items.answer: Person specification

items.stem: Define the term 'induction training'.
items.answer: Training given to new employees to introduce them to the business, its procedures, facilities and colleagues.
items.markingKey: 2 marks: full definition – Training given to new employees to introduce them to the business, its procedures, facilities and colleagues. 1 mark: partial definition or a relevant example only. [2]

items.stem: Explain why induction training is important.
items.answer: It helps new employees become productive quickly, understand rules such as health and safety, and feel welcome, which reduces the chance of them leaving early.
items.markingKey: 1 mark faster productivity; 1 mark procedures/safety; 1 mark lower early labour turnover. [3]

items.stem: Explain one advantage and one disadvantage of off-the-job training.
items.answer: Advantage: experts can teach a wider range of skills without workplace distractions. Disadvantage: it is expensive and the employee is not producing while away.
items.markingKey: 1 mark advantage, 1 mark explanation; 1 mark disadvantage, 1 mark explanation. [4]

items.stem: Define the term 'labour turnover'.
items.answer: The rate at which employees leave a business, usually measured as the number leaving in a year as a percentage of the average number employed.
items.markingKey: 2 marks: full definition – The rate at which employees leave a business, usually measured as the number leaving in a year as a percentage of the average number employed. 1 mark: partial definition or a relevant example only. [2]

items.stem: Explain two costs to a business of high labour turnover.
items.answer: The costs of recruiting and training replacements; and lower productivity and quality while new staff learn, with possible damage to customer service and morale.
items.markingKey: 2 × (1 mark cost, 1 mark explanation). [4]

items.stem: Explain the difference between redundancy and dismissal.
items.answer: Redundancy is when the job is no longer needed, for example because of falling demand or automation; dismissal is when the employee is removed because of their own conduct or performance.
items.markingKey: 1 mark redundancy; 1 mark dismissal. [2]

items.answer: Points to develop for Bosphorus Home: labour turnover measures how many staff leave; low pay compared with competitors; poor working conditions or management; lack of training or promotion opportunities.
items.markingKey: AO1 Knowledge [1]: labour turnover measures how many staff leave. AO2 Application [1]: point linked to Bosphorus Home (household appliance manufacturing). items.answer: Points to develop for Siam Ready Meals: high turnover means many staff leave each year; higher recruitment and training costs; lower productivity and quality of ready meals; lower morale among remaining staff.

items.answer: A legal agreement between an employer and an employee that sets out the terms and conditions of employment, such as pay, hours and duties.

items.stem: Explain two benefits to a business of offering flexible working.
items.answer: It can match staff numbers to busy periods, reducing costs; and it attracts and keeps employees, such as parents, who want flexible hours, improving motivation.
items.markingKey: 2 × (1 mark benefit, 1 mark explanation). [4]

items.stem: Explain why a contract of employment is important to both the employer and the employee.
items.answer: It sets out the rights and duties of each side, such as pay, hours and notice, which reduces disputes and gives the employee legal protection.
items.markingKey: 1 mark terms set out; 1 mark benefit to employer; 1 mark benefit to employee. [3]
